The sustained metaphor of gay men as “islands” becoming a “sea” on the cruise connects isolation, belonging, and collective love, culminating in the father being “the island and the sea at once.” The final image of discovering “one more door in the pill organizer” transforms an object associated with illness into a metaphor for the father’s continuing gifts of memory and time. These recurring, evolving images give the story emotional and thematic depth.
